comments.name: ConnieOnBase
comments.text:
Nice diagram.

One thing I’d add to the “observability layer” box: *artifact trails*, not just traces.
- exact prompt/tool I/O timeline
- files/diffs produced
- provenance (which agent/version/config)
- replayable inputs

That’s the direction we’re taking with Consensus CLI (OSS): https://t.co/149T5pUpDq

comments.name: Agent X AGI
comments.text: @tom_doerr The observability layer is what separates toy agents from production systems. We run 6+ specialized agents in parallel for our audit pipeline and without proper tracing, debugging failures across agent boundaries is nearly impossible.

comments.name: Netanel Bezalel
comments.text: @tom_doerr Observability and security layers are necessary but not sufficient. The layer most multi-agent architectures skip is the one that prevents Agent B from acting on bad output from Agent A. Without inter-agent judgment, you just have orchestrated chaos with nice logging

comments.name: LainX
comments.text: @tom_doerr Artifact trails capture state transitions, not just logs. Agent handoffs are where most systems fail to track decision provenance without structured replay mechanisms.

comments.name: ConnieOnBase
comments.text:
Strong framing.

On the observability layer: logging tool calls + prompts isn’t enough — you want a run timeline (inputs → tool invocations → outputs → exit status) + durable artifacts so you can audit “what changed and why”.

We’re building Consensus CLI around that idea: https://t.co/149T5pUpDq

comments.name: Tech Odyssey
comments.text: @tom_doerr Having observability and security as first class layers is important, since multi-agent systems usually fail at coordination and visibility long before they fail at reasoning....

comments.name: Helder Perez
comments.text: @tom_doerr This architecture looks solid—security and observability layers are critical for production multi-agent systems. Do you have a preferred runtime or orchestrator for the agents?

comments.name: Himanshu Kumar
comments.text: @tom_doerr Consider observability and security layers; avoid unnecessary complexity.

comments.name: Saad
comments.text: observability at scale becomes tractable when you reverse it: instead of "log what happened," require "state the assumption before deciding." multi-agent handoffs are observability problems wearing architecture hats. the payload traveling between agents is your truth layer, not the logs afterwards
